tagline: Down the California coast, one cliff town at a time.
intro: Route 1 starts in the redwoods outside Leggett and follows Cottaneva Creek out to the sea. At Fort Bragg it becomes Main Street and bridges the Noyo River. Farther south it crosses the Golden Gate Bridge with US 101, then keeps to the coast through Davenport and Santa Cruz.

Big Sur was the slow part. San Quentin set up convict camps there, paying inmates 35 cents a day and trimming their sentences, and the road opened on June 17, 1937, after 18 years and 33 bridges. For about 72 miles it hugs the cliffs.

moments.title: Fort Bragg
moments.text: At Glass Beach, waves wore discarded bottles and other glass from the town’s former dump into small, smooth pieces.

moments.title: Davenport
moments.text: Agua Puerca Creek, whose name means muddy water, silted up Captain Davenport's lumber wharf until steamers could not tie up, and the town kept his name anyway.

moments.title: Lucia
moments.text: Ten cabins stand on a 300-foot cliff above the Pacific, on land the Harlan family homesteaded in 1885 and refused to sell to William Randolph Hearst.

practical: Landslides and erosion along the coast, Big Sur especially, have closed stretches of the road for long periods.
